abstract: A Lean 4 development of the counterexamples of Hegarty, Ognissanti and Wedin (arXiv:2610.03229) to two conjectures and a theorem of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo on heterogeneous Hegselmann–Krause dynamics. n agents with real opinions and positive bounds r_1, ..., r_n update synchronously, x(t+1) = A(x(t)) x(t), where row i of A(y) averages uniformly over the neighbourhood N_i(y): the j with |y_i - y_j| <= r_i in the SBC model (synchronized bounded confidence) and <= r_j in the SBI model (synchronized bounded influence). Conjecture 2.2 says the proximity digraph is constant after a finite time; Conjecture 2.3 says every trajectory reaches a fixed state or is eventually pseudo-stable (the agents split into two non-empty classes, fixed at their limits or moving strictly towards them from one side); Theorem 6.4(iv) says a trajectory whose digraph is constant from some time on is eventually pseudo-stable. For the four systems of the source (SBC with seven agents and rate -1/6; SBI with seven agents and rate (1 - sqrt 5)/8; SBC with six agents; a second SBI system with seven agents) the development proves the closed form x(t) = x_inf + c lambda^t v for every t, the neighbourhood of every agent at every t (alternating with the parity of t at the middle agent of the two seven-agent alternating systems, the same at every t in the other two), convergence, and that no trajectory is ever frozen or pseudo-stable after any time towards any vector, since four agents alternate sides of their limits. Hence Conjectures 2.2 and 2.3 fail in each model, and Theorem 6.4(iv) fails in each model, both in its literal reading and in the reading that also admits a fixed state. Two smaller constant-digraph systems found in this development, five SBC agents with rate (1 - sqrt 2)/3 and six SBI agents with rate (13 - sqrt 249)/40, have one real negative mode. A five-agent SBI system of this development has a complex pair of modes: the offsets of its three moving agents follow a rational averaging map from an algebraic initial offset (the real root of a cubic), its digraph is constant, it converges, and every moving agent is strictly on both sides of its limit in every five consecutive times. So Conjecture 2.3 and Theorem 6.4(iv) fail with five agents in either model. A five-agent SBC family shows that these failures persist with positive, unequal bounds whose ratio of largest to smallest is below any 1 + epsilon. Along all four source systems the final value at constant topology (Definition 3.1) of every x(t) is the limit, and in the two constant-digraph source systems the per-step convergence factor (Definition 6.1) of every agent with nonzero offset is identically the negative rate, so it converges to no non-negative number. On the positive side, Lemma 4.2 (the equi-topology neighbourhood preserves the proximity digraph) and Lemma 4.8 (a convergent trajectory whose limit has every equi-topology distance positive eventually has the digraph of its limit, the limit as its final value at constant topology, and an equilibrium limit) are proved for arbitrary bounds; the limits of the two constant-digraph systems satisfy that hypothesis, and those of the two alternating systems violate it. For the source's two spectator systems (nine SBC agents with a spectator and two beacons; eight SBI agents with a spectator) the closed forms, the constant tables and the spectator's side are proved, and along the five-agent SBC and six-agent SBI single-mode systems too the final value at constant topology is the limit and the per-step factor is the rate. Not claimed: Theorem 6.4(iii) in full, Conjecture 2.1 (convergence of every trajectory), or that any minimality result is formalized in Lean.
